correctness.rationale: On AB, counting common AA and BB neighbors gives the stated sum of two incidence Gram matrices. The four constant/mean-zero tensor sectors give squared singular values Ω², α², β² and 0 with dimensions 1, p−1, q−1 and (p−1)(q−1). For p,q≥3 the coupling rank is p+q−1, so the full zero multiplicity is N−2(p+q−1); frequency collisions add multiplicities. Projecting an AB basis vector onto those sectors gives the four weights of the cosine formula. If w is the zero weight, 1−R≤2(1−w), |R|≤1 and hence 1−|R|²≤4(1−w). In the uniform three-layer subspace the hop counts give couplings √(2q(p−1)) and √(2p(q−1)); the AA-to-BB amplitude equals their product times (cos(Ωt)−1)/Ω². The maximum is one exactly when the couplings are equal, i.e. p=q, and occurs at odd half-periods. The cross-shore matrix entries are constant under independent shore permutations and their amplitude is the collective one divided by the square root of the product of layer sizes. These are all-size checks. The recorded exact checks for 3≤p,q≤7 are finite corroboration, not the basis of the verdict.
